scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Gas is the unit of computation
Explorers (e.g. Etherscan) show status, fee, sender, contract called, token transfers…
scenes.vo: Lifecycle: create to sign to broadcast to mempool (waiting) to included in a block to confirmed to final. Ethereum the price has a base fee (burned) plus a priority tip (to get included sooner). Gas price is quoted in gwei (1 gwei equals 0.000000001 ETH). low-nonce transaction blocks all later ones until it confirms or is replaced (same nonce, higher fee). reversed. It differs by chain, and layer twos have their own rules (Module 5). First, Gas is the unit of computation. Cost equals gas used times gas price. On. Next, Nonce: each account's transactions are numbered in order. A stuck. Then, Failed transactions still cost gas. The network did the computation even though the result was reverted. Also, Finality: the point after which a transaction can't realistically be. And finally, Explorers (for example Etherscan) show status, fee, sender, contract called, token transfers and logs.
scenes.cap: Lifecycle: create → sign → broadcast → mempool (waiting) → included in a block → confirmed → final. Ethereum the price has a base fee (burned) plus a priority tip (to get included sooner). Gas price is quoted in gwei (1 gwei = 0.000000001 ETH). low-nonce transaction blocks all later ones until it confirms or is replaced (same nonce, higher fee). reversed. It differs by chain, and L2s have their own rules (Module 5). First, Gas is the unit of computation. Cost = gas used × gas price. On. Next, Nonce: each account's transactions are numbered in order. A stuck. Then, Failed transactions still cost gas. The network did the computation even though the result was reverted. Also, Finality: the point after which a transaction can't realistically be. And finally, Explorers (e.g. Etherscan) show status, fee, sender, contract called, token transfers and logs.

scenes.title: Worked example
steps: A swap uses 150,000 gas at 20 gwei
The same swap during congestion at 80 gwei costs $36.
If you're compounding $1.50 of rewards, the gas costs more than the rewards.
That's why position size matters on-chain.
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. A swap uses 150,000 gas at 20 gwei: 150,000 times 20 equals 3,000,000 gwei equals 0.003 ETH. At $3,000/ETH that's $9. The same swap during congestion at 80 gwei costs $36. If you're compounding $1.50 of rewards, the gas costs more than the rewards. That's why position size matters on-chain.
scenes.cap: Let's work an example, step by step. A swap uses 150,000 gas at 20 gwei: 150,000 × 20 = 3,000,000 gwei = 0.003 ETH. At $3,000/ETH that's $9. scenes.title: Checklist
items: I check the fee estimate before signing
I know how to find my transaction on an explorer
I know a stuck transaction can be sped up or cancelled with the same nonce

scenes.q: Your transaction reverted. Did you pay?
scenes.a: Yes, for the gas used up to the point of failure.
scenes.vo: Question one. Your transaction reverted. Did you pay? [[pause 4]] The answer: Yes, for the gas used up to the point of failure.

scenes.q: 200,000 gas at 10 gwei with ETH at $2,500 costs?
scenes.vo: Question two. 200,000 gas at 10 gwei with ETH at $2,500 costs? [[pause 4]] The answer: 2,000,000 gwei equals 0.002 ETH = $5.

scenes.q: Why are your newer transactions all pending?
scenes.a: An earlier nonce is stuck. Replace or speed it up, and the rest follow.
